title: Beyond the Title: How the DeW Retreat Is Redefining Leadership and Community in Dentistry
html:
At DeW Life’s 10th anniversary celebration, women across dentistry came together to explore courage, entrepreneurship, personal growth, and the power of genuine connection.

What happens when you bring together a room full of accomplished women in dentistry and take away the very thing that often defines them professionally—their titles?

Something remarkable.

From November 12–14, 2026, DeW Life celebrated its 10th anniversary at The Ballantyne in Charlotte, North Carolina. Over three days, women from across the dental industry gathered for a retreat centered on leadership, personal growth, entrepreneurship, and meaningful connection.

For those unfamiliar with DeW, short for Dental Entrepreneur Woman, it is more than an organization or an annual event. It is a community built on the belief that women can achieve more when they support, encourage, and learn from one another.

Throughout the retreat, one thing became clear: DeW is not simply bringing women together. It is changing the way they connect.

Beyond the Business Card

If you’ve ever watched The Ellen DeGeneres Show, you probably remember how Ellen could get an entire audience on its feet, dancing and laughing before the conversation even began. At moments, the DeW Retreat carried that same infectious energy.

Women were dancing, laughing, and celebrating together. At other moments, the room was moved to tears as deeply personal stories were shared. It was this balance of joy and vulnerability that made the experience so memorable.

That authenticity extended to the way women introduced themselves.

Instead of prominently displaying company names or job titles, attendees wore badges highlighting their CliftonStrengths, a framework designed to help individuals understand their natural talents.

It was a subtle but powerful shift.

Conversations weren’t centered on who held the highest position or worked for the largest company. They were about what mattered to each woman, the challenges she faced, and who she wanted to become.

A business owner could sit beside someone contemplating her first entrepreneurial venture. A seasoned leader could share the same uncertainties as someone just beginning her career.

The common ground wasn’t a job title. It was the shared experience of navigating ambition, change, relationships, and personal growth.

The Courage to Write Your Next Chapter

One of the retreat’s central themes was courage—not necessarily extraordinary acts of bravery, but the everyday decisions that shape our lives.

For some women, that meant considering leaving a stable career to pursue an entrepreneurial dream. For others, it meant setting boundaries, redefining success, or recognizing that the path they were following no longer aligned with the life they wanted to build.

Throughout the retreat, attendees were encouraged to consider a powerful question:

What courageous decisions does the next season of your life require?

Another message resonated just as strongly: “No” is a full sentence.

For women balancing professional expectations, family responsibilities, and the desire to support everyone around them, recognizing when not to take on more can be just as important as identifying the next opportunity.

The conversations also encouraged women to reflect on their past, present, and future selves—and to understand the stories of those sitting beside them.

What is her passion? What is her mission? What is her why?

In an industry where conferences often revolve around products, business transactions, and professional advancement, DeW offered something different: the opportunity to connect beyond résumés and recognize the person behind the professional.

When Women Invest in Women

At the heart of the retreat were Anne Duffy, founder of DeW, and Kristie Boltz, this year’s master of ceremonies, whose openness helped set the tone for the gathering.

Both shared personal experiences, challenges, and defining moments from their journeys, reinforcing that leadership doesn’t require projecting perfection.

Their message centered on generosity, authenticity, and the fulfillment that comes from helping others succeed.

Perhaps one of the most powerful examples unfolded spontaneously during the retreat.

One woman offered to contribute money toward helping another woman pursue her dream of starting a business. Almost immediately, others began pledging their own contributions, even though no recipient had yet been identified. What started as one person’s gesture quickly became a collective effort.

Then, a woman in the audience stood up and shared that she had been dreaming of starting her own company.

Before anyone knew who would receive the support, women were already willing to invest in someone else’s future.

That is what genuine empowerment looks like—not just encouraging someone to pursue her dreams, but helping create the opportunity for her to do so.

A Community That Extends Beyond the Retreat

Throughout the weekend, women described how relationships formed through DeW had evolved into some of their closest friendships and most meaningful mentorships.

And when unexpected travel disruptions left some attendees struggling to return home, that sense of community became especially tangible.

Local DeW members in Charlotte opened their homes, offered rides, and helped fellow attendees find places to stay. Others checked in, shared updates, and made sure no one was left navigating the uncertainty alone.

In a message following the retreat, the DeW Life team reflected on the generosity shown by its members.

The women who had spent the weekend discussing the importance of community were now putting those values into practice.

It was a reminder that meaningful relationships aren’t defined by the number of contacts exchanged at an event. They’re defined by what happens when someone needs help.

When Inspiration Becomes Action

The impact of DeW doesn’t end when the retreat is over. Sometimes, it becomes the beginning of an entirely new movement.

For Edna Abreu, that is exactly what happened.

Following last year’s DeW Retreat, Abreu recognized a need within the dental industry for a dedicated community supporting Latinas. Shortly afterward, she founded Latinas in Dentistry, a growing professional network empowering Latina women across the dental field, including students, dental assistants, hygienists, office managers, and dentists.

One year later, her journey came full circle.

At DeW Life’s 10th anniversary retreat, Abreu delivered her first DeW Talk, reflecting on overcoming self-doubt, recognizing her potential, and finding the courage to pursue new opportunities.

In an Instagram post following the event, Abreu credited Duffy, DeW’s founder, for believing in her and helping open doors she hadn’t imagined possible.

Her message to other women was powerful:

“There is a seat with your name on it. Go take it.”

This year, members of the Latinas in Dentistry community were there supporting Abreu as she took the stage.

One year ago, she was inspired by the women in the room. This year, she returned with a community of women she had inspired herself.

Her story illustrates the ripple effect of mentorship and encouragement—and how one person’s belief in another can create opportunities that extend far beyond a single individual.

More Than a Retreat, a Movement

As dentistry continues to evolve, conversations about innovation, technology, practice growth, and clinical advancement will remain essential. But so should conversations about the people driving that progress.

The DeW Retreat serves as a reminder that professional development is not limited to acquiring new skills or advancing a career. It also involves building self-awareness, strengthening relationships, finding purpose, and developing the courage to make meaningful decisions.

Sometimes the most valuable takeaway from a professional event isn’t a new business opportunity or a lesson in leadership. It’s the realization that no one has to navigate her next chapter alone.

The true impact of a movement isn’t measured by how many women it brings into a room, but by how many leave inspired to open doors for others.

That is what makes DeW more than a retreat. It makes DeW a movement.

The next DeW Life Retreat is scheduled for November 11–13, 2027. To learn more about DeW Life, membership opportunities, and upcoming events, visit dew.life.
